region.text: the province of Herat, whose central plain (38 cells round Herat city, 33.7-34.9 N, 61.7-62.9 E) the principality's own shape left out

events.note: Sultan Ahmad Khan, then Shah Nawaz Khan, ruled Herat until 'On May 27 Dost Mohammad made a final assault on Herat' and 'The city was conquered by the Emirate of Afghanistan, ending the Principality of Herat' (1863). The compile leaves the 38 cells round Herat city to nobody in 1860-1869, because the principality's shape lacks them and the Afghan gain of 1863 only takes the principality's own cells; giving them to the principality from 1860 lets the 1863 gain carry them to Afghanistan.

region.text: the provinces of Trieste and Gorizia, which the Veneto 'Friuli' region of the gain of October 1866 wrongly sweeps in

events.note: The Treaty of Vienna of 3 October 1866 gave Italy 'modern Veneto, parts of Friuli and the city of Mantua'; Italy's annexation of 'Trentino, the remainder of Friuli and Trieste' came 'at the end of World War I'. The ledger gain of 1866 resolves the whole Friuli region, which includes Trieste and the Gorizia province, so about 3 cells go back to Austria.

region.text: the Taiping shape of 1860 minus the Taiping shape of 1861: Hubei land the Taiping no longer hold

events.note: Land that Cliopatria's Taiping shape of 1861 leaves out and the 1860 shape had: the Taiping Rebellion page has the Xiang Army taking back the middle Yangtze ('In December 1856 Qing forces retook Wuchang for the final time', 'In May 1858, the Xiang Army captured Jiujiang and then the rest of Jiangxi by September', 'In 1861 ... union.text: the part of Cliopatria's oversize Panthay shape of 1860 inside China: Kunming and east Yunnan, the Sichuan basin and the Chongqing and Guizhou edges, which the Qing held (the smaller Panthay state, cut to the Dali basin and Lijiang by its dossier, still wins its own cells by the size rule)

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1860 Qing shape plus the Qing part of the Panthay shape (Kunming, east Yunnan, Sichuan basin)

keyframe_overrides.why: The Panthay dossier cuts Cliopatria's Panthay shape (408,545 km2, east to 107.7 E and north to 31.6 N) to the Dali basin and Lijiang, but the Qing keyframe, Cliopatria's own, leaves that whole shape out, so about 1,285 cells (Chengdu, Leshan, Ya'an, Yibin, Luzhou, Kunming, Qujing, Zhaotong, Mengzi, parts of Chongqing and Guizhou) belong to nobody in every year 1860-1867. The Panthay Rebellion page puts the Sultanate in the west: 'gaining control of Dali in 1856', 'The eight years from 1860 to 1868 were the heyday of the Sultanate', and says Hui from provinces 'not in rebellion, like Sichuan and Zhejiang' acted as go-betweens; Kunming is the provincial capital that was attacked and sacked several times, and Ma Rulong, the Hui defector, fought for the Qing in central and west Yunnan in the 1860s. So Kunming, east Yunnan and Sichuan were Qing land, not nobody's.
